While Ruby continues to not have this the default, user can opt into it using the `RUBYOPT` environment variable. To make RuboCop behave correctly when doing that, offer a config value to say how literals behave by default.

The most egregious cop `Style/FrozenStringLiteralComment` can already be configured appropriately by setting `EnforcedStyle` to `never`. This makes if possible to also change behaviour about cops that concern themselves with string literals (primarily `MutableConstant`).

-----------------

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

* [x] The PR relates to *only* one subject with a clear title and description in grammatically correct, complete sentences.
* [x] Wrote [good commit messages][1].
* [ ] Commit message starts with `[Fix #issue-number]` (if the related issue exists).
* [x] Feature branch is up-to-date with `master` (if not - rebase it).
* [x] Squashed related commits together.
* [x] Added tests.
* [x] Ran `bundle exec rake default`. It executes all tests and runs RuboCop on its own code.
* [x] Added an entry (file) to the [changelog folder](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/master/changelog/) named `{change_type}_{change_description}.md` if the new code introduces user-observable changes. See [changelog entry format](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#changelog-entry-format) for details.

[1]: https://chris.beams.io/posts/git-commit/

issue_context.title: Style/EmptyLiteral with --enable=frozen-string-literal flag
issue_context.body:
## Expected behavior

`String.new` should not be auto-corrected with `''` when have `Style/EmptyLiteral` enabled and run with the `--enable=frozen-string-literal` flag.

## Actual behavior

`String.new` will be replaced with `''`

## Steps to reproduce the problem

1. add a ruby file with a line `String.new`.
2. run `export RUBYOPT="--enable-frozen-string-literal"` in command line.
3. run auto-correct on the ruby file.
4. `String.new` will be replaced with `''`

## RuboCop version

```
$ [bundle exec] rubocop -V
1.53.0 (using Parser 3.2.2.3, rubocop-ast 1.29.0, running on ruby 3.0.0) [x86_64-linux]
  - rubocop-performance 1.15.0
  - rubocop-rails 2.16.1
```

## Possible fixes:

We can check `RUBYOPT` in `frozen_string_literals_enabled?` method.
Ex:
```rb
return true if ENV['RUBYOPT'].include?('--enable-frozen-string-literal')
```
https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/a7b7c5f95ac32612b0f9c0a9661281b5633ae07b/lib/rubocop/cop/mixin/frozen_string_literal.rb#L21-L41
comments: Hhm, environment variables given to `ruby` command are for runtime information, so I wonder about their use in static analysis.

How about adding an option for rubocop to know that `frozen_string_literals` is always enabled in this project, so that `String.new` will never be replaced with `''` while `Hash.new` will still be replaced with `{}`
You can use `AllCops/StringLiteralsFrozenByDefault: true` in the next RuboCop version for this.

review_comments: Typo since introduction, was always true for most users since `Enabled` came from the department.

This function says strings are frozen when no comment is present in preparation of `Style/FrozenStringLiteralComment` doing its autocorrect. Introduced in #9773. I don't love this since it now gets complicated when the default changes. The change to the function works but I feel pretty meh about it.

Why no `autocorrect_incompatible_with`? `EmptyLiteral` comes before `FrozenStringLiteralComment` alphabetically. I played around with letting cops say their autocorrect is more important than others but didn't like how that turned out.

I would rather get rid of this workaround entirely. The user runs unsafe autocorrect and should not be surprised when things break.
